summary.title: Writing a Markdown Compiler – Part 1
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build the tokenizer (lexical analysis) stage of a simple Markdown-to-HTML compiler in Ruby, using scanner objects and Minitest specs.
keywords: compiler structure tokenizer parser code generator
takeaways: A compiler is a black box that translates input in one language to output in another; transpilers are compilers too.
A tokenizer turns raw characters into typed tokens such as UNDERSCORE, STAR, NEWLINE, TEXT and EOF.
Scanner objects each match specific tokens, and scan_one_token tries them in turn, returning a null token when nothing matches.
The null object pattern removes nil checks and conditionals from scanner code.
The pipeline is tokenizer, then parser producing an AST, then code generator, so each stage can be tested or swapped independently.
summary.summary: This first part of a beezwax blog series introduces compilers and builds the tokenizer for a tiny Markdown subset (paragraphs, emphasis, bold) that outputs HTML. The author explains the three-stage compiler structure (tokenizer, parser, code generator) and describes an object-oriented design with Token objects, a Tokenizer that recursively scans input, and scanners such as a single-character scanner and a text scanner. Tests are written with Minitest, and the full source is in a GitHub repository. Parsing and code generation are deferred to Parts 2 and 3.
